runbook: R-18 / R-19 (independent oracle, blind to the change under test)

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Abyssal Mask's curse is a TYPED amplifier: +12%, magic damage only. 'from all sources' widens the set of attackers, not the set of damage types.

sources_quoted.text: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable mark is an UNTYPED amplifier: +7% to every damage type.
The cached atomizer independently types the Unmake amp as damage.magic with parameter 12 percent (and a 700-unit range), corroborating S1's magic-only scope.

sources_quoted.text: Imperial Mandate stats: abilityPower 60, abilityHaste 15; no typed-damage atom for the Command mark.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: Nothing in the cached data types the Vulnerable mark to a damage school; S2's plain text ('damage they take from all sources by 7%') governs -> untyped.

sources_quoted.text: Table covers resistance mitigation, penetration/reduction composition, stat growth, AS, ability haste, DoT, on-hit, burn, grievous wounds, shields, grey health, revive, BIS, stat rounding, Terminus/BC ramps.
sources_quoted.rule_extracted: NEGATIVE result, recorded for honesty: math-foundations.md contains no damage-amplifier row at all. It neither prescribes the amp stacking convention nor the typed/untyped scope. The scope rule therefore rests entirely on the cached wiki text S1-S4.

independent_computation.note: The golden scenario's setup (champions, roster, items, level) lives in scripts/ and tests/, which this runbook forbids reading. The computation below is therefore structural: it solves for the damage split that each candidate value implies and asks which split is consistent with the sourced rules S1-S4. The system is exactly determined, so the split is unique per hypothesis.
independent_computation.model_from_sources: total = 1.07 * (NonMagic + 1.12 * Magic)  -- S2 applies 1.07 to every type, S1 applies 1.12 to the magic type only. (Amps compose multiplicatively; with only one amp per type here, additive-vs-multiplicative stacking is not exercised.)

step_1_delta.algebra: old - new = 222.5. Under the only 12%-scope hypotheses that fit, the delta is the untyped-mark-compounded curse on one damage component: delta = 1.07 * 0.12 * C  =>  C = 222.5 / 0.1284 = 1732.87.

step_2_hypothesis_H1_old_leaked_the_type.statement: OLD applied the magic-only 12% to the whole packet: old = 1.07 * 1.12 * (NonMagic + Magic). NEW applies it only to the magic slice: new = 1.07 * (NonMagic + 1.12 * Magic).
step_2_hypothesis_H1_old_leaked_the_type.solve: NonMagic = 222.5 / (1.07*0.12) = 1732.87 ; total pre-amp post-mitigation D = 2406.2 / 1.1984 = 2007.84 ; Magic = D - NonMagic = 274.98
step_2_hypothesis_H1_old_leaked_the_type.verdict_on_H1: Under H1 the OLD value violates S1/S3: it charges the magic-typed 12% against 1732.87 of non-magic damage. The NEW value obeys both S1 (12% on magic only) and S2 (7% on everything), and the curse still contributes 35.3 damage.

step_3_competing_hypothesis_H2_new_dropp.statement: The same delta equation is satisfied by the mirror hypothesis: OLD = 1.07*(NonMagic + 1.12*Magic) with Magic = 1732.87, NonMagic = 307.98, and NEW = 1.07*(NonMagic + Magic) -- i.e. the curse dropped out entirely (magic fraction 0.849).
why_rejected: S1 states the curse amplifies magic damage 'from all sources'. No sourced condition in the cached data removes it for a roster ally's damage; the only stated gate is the 700-unit range, which a modelled teamfight satisfies for every other aura in the corpus.

H2 makes Abyssal Mask inert for this leaf: the curse would contribute exactly 0.0 to breakdown[0]. A scenario named 'mandate_abyssal_CURSE_roster' whose pinned leaf no longer contains any curse contribution would stop testing the thing it is named for.

The scenario pairs precisely one untyped amp (S2, 7%) with one typed amp (S1, 12%). That pairing is the discriminating test for amp SCOPE. Only H1's new value exercises both scopes distinctly (1.07 on 1732.87 of non-magic, 1.07*1.12 on 274.98 of magic); H2's new value collapses to a single untyped 7% and discriminates nothing.

Direction of a typed-amp defect: applying a magic-only multiplier to a full mixed packet is the standard over-count failure (the same class as the item-literal over-statements CLAUDE.md rule 5 exists to prevent). H2 would instead be a regression that silently zeroes a live item passive.

step_4_hypotheses_ruled_out_arithmetical: Multiplicative -> additive amp stacking (1.1984 -> 1.19): ratio 1.0071, far from the observed 1.10189. Rejected.
Additive -> multiplicative (1.19 -> 1.1984): wrong sign (damage would rise). Rejected.
Double-counted curse from two roster holders (1.12^2 -> 1.12): ratio 1.12, outside the rounding band [1.101843, 1.101939]. Rejected.
Dropping the Vulnerable mark entirely (1.07 factor): 2183.7 * 1.07 = 2336.6 != 2406.2. Rejected.

Curse modelled as a 12% magic-RESIST shred instead of a 12% magic-damage amp: matching the observed ratio requires target MR = 15.6, which no level-appropriate champion in data/champions.json carries; and docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 2.2 shows reduction and amplification are distinct engine stages. Rejected.
Curse leaking onto TRUE damage only: requires the packet to be 86% true damage. Implausible and still a leak of the magic-typed amp (same verdict direction anyway).
independent_computation.conclusion: Independently recomputed correct value = 2183.7 (= 1.07 * (1732.87 non-magic + 1.12 * 274.98 magic)). The old 2406.2 equals 1.07 * 1.12 * 2007.84, i.e. Abyssal Mask's magic-typed 12% charged against the entire packet including its non-magic 1732.87.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The scenario's setup is not reachable from data/ (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains 22 corpus scenarios, none of them 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster'), so the damage split could not be observed directly - only inverted from the two candidate totals. The delta equation delta = 1.07 * 0.12 * C is symmetric between 'the 12% leaked onto the non-magic component' (H1) and 'the 12% was dropped from the magic component' (H2); the two are numerically indistinguishable and were separated on sourced-rule and test-design grounds (step_3), not on arithmetic.
residual_uncertainty.what_would_settle_it: The scenario's damage-type split for breakdown[0]. If breakdown[0]'s pre-amp post-mitigation magic damage is ~275 (13.7% magic), the new value is right. If it is ~1733 (84.9% magic) and an Abyssal Mask holder is ally-side and in range, the old value was right and the new one zeroes a live passive.
